questions.question_text: What is public speaking, as defined in the chapter?

options.text: Only giving formal speeches on a stage with a microphone
The art of communicating ideas, information, or emotions to an audience in any setting
A skill that only applies to professional presenters
A talent that cannot be learned or improvedCorrect Answer:B. The art of communicating ideas, information, or emotions to an audience in any setting

questions.question_text: According to the chapter, how can public speaking impact academic success for high school students?

options.text: It has no effect on grades or teacher impressions
It can boost grades by improving presentations and class discussions
It only helps in extracurricular activities, not academics
It guarantees perfect test scores without studyingCorrect Answer:B. It can boost grades by improving presentations and class discussions

questions.question_text: What is one reason the chapter highlights communication as powerful for building leadership?

options.text: It prevents any conflicts from happening in a group
It allows leaders to motivate, solve problems, and guide others with their words
It ensures everyone agrees with the leader instantly
It is only useful for leaders in professional settings, not in schoolCorrect Answer:B. It allows leaders to motivate, solve problems, and guide others with their words

questions.question_text: How does the chapter suggest students start overcoming initial fears of public speaking?

options.text: By avoiding speaking situations altogether
By acknowledging the fear and starting with small, low-pressure speaking moments
By waiting until they feel completely confident before trying
By only speaking in front of large audiences to get over nerves quicklyCorrect Answer:B. By acknowledging the fear and starting with small, low-pressure speaking moments

questions.question_text: What does the SMART framework for setting communication goals stand for, as explained in the chapter?

options.text: Simple, Manageable, Attractive, Realistic, Timely
Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-Bound
Strong, Motivated, Active, Reliable, Targeted
Smart, Meaningful, Ambitious, Routine, TemporaryCorrect Answer:B. Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-Bound
